question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}x-z=0 \\ x+y+3z=2 \\ 3x-2y+z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & b \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ a & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ c \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+0y-z=0 \\ x+y+3z=2 \\ 3x-2y+z=4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=3,\,b=-1,\,c=2.$
